Abstract: BackgroundTambotatug pelitecan (known as Tam-Peli, a new antibody–drug conjugate that targets the immune-checkpoint molecule B7-H3) showed promising clinical efficacy in patients with relapsed extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer in early-phase trials. MethodsIn this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial, we assigned eligible patients with small-cell lung cancer that had progressed after first-line platinum-based therapy in a 1:1 ratio to receive tambotatug pelitecan or topotecan. The primary end point was overall survival. The key secondary end points were progression-free survival and objective response as assessed by investigators. Here, we report the results from the prespecified interim analysis. ResultsA total of 451 patients underwent randomization: 225 were assigned to receive tambotatug pelitecan and 226 to receive topotecan. Overall survival was significantly longer with tambotatug pelitecan than with topotecan — a median of 13.3 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.1 to could not be estimated), as compared with 9.4 months (95% CI, 7.7 to 10.5); the stratified hazard ratio for death was 0.46 (95% CI, 0.35 to 0.62; P<0.001). Treatment with tambotatug pelitecan also resulted in significantly longer progression-free survival than treatment with topotecan (median, 7.4 months [95% CI, 6.1 to 7.6] vs. 2.8 months [95% CI, 1.8 to 3.0]; stratified hazard ratio, 0.29 [95% CI, 0.23 to 0.37]; P<0.001). A confirmed objective response occurred in 59.1% of the patients in the tambotatug pelitecan group, as compared with 9.7% of those in the topotecan group (P<0.001). The overall incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher was lower with tambotatug pelitecan than with topotecan (55.4% vs. 77.9%). ConclusionsAmong patients with relapsed small-cell lung cancer after platinum-based therapy, treatment with tambotatug pelitecan resulted in longer overall survival, longer progression-free survival, and a higher percentage of patients with an objective response than treatment with topotecan, with a lower incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher. (Funded by the Innovative Drug Research and Development National Science and Technology Major Project and MediLink Therapeutics; TAISHAN-302 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06612151.)
Author: Zhao, Yuanyuan
Title: Tambotatug Pelitecan in Small-Cell Lung Cancer after Platinum-Based Therapy

Abstract: BACKGROUND: Firearm injuries (FAIs) continue to be a global public health problem possessing substantial emotional, physical and financial burdens on hospital resources. Although FAIs are rare in children, their incidence is gradually increasing. AIM: The aim of this study was to evaluate various aspects of FAI in children that were managed at a tertiary care centre located in the rural part of India. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This clinical observational study of children <18 years of age, all due to FAI, was conducted at a tertiary care centre located in the rural part of India. Data of all children admitted with FAI over 4 years from January 2016 to December 2019 were collected. Recorded data included age, sex, motive (intentional/unintentional) and circumstances leading to injury, type and license status of firearm used, time of injury, pre‑hospital care, mode of transport to hospital, duration between injury and arrival to hospital, body parts and organs injured, trauma scores, management, complications, length of hospital stay and outcomes. The recorded data were entered into a worksheet and analysed. RESULTS: Out of 283 cases of FAI admitted, only 24 were children with age <18 years (8.48%). The mean age was 12.66 years (male:female = 2.4:1). Sixteen were intentional (66.67%) and eight were unintentional (33.33%). The family feud was the most common reason in case of intentional FAI (43.75%), and mishandling was the most common reason in case of unintentional FAI. Country made gun was the most common firearm used (62.5%). The chest and upper back were the most common sites of injury (54.16%). Intercostal drainage tube insertion was the most common surgical procedure performed (33.33%). There were three mortalities (12.5%). CONCLUSION: The present study found that intentional FAIs in children were more common than unintentional FAIs with family feuds and mishandling being the most common causes, respectively. The unlicensed country‑made gun was the most common firearm causing injury in children.
Author: Amit, Chaudhary
Title: Firearm Injuries in Children: Four‑year Experience from a Rural Tertiary Care Centre of Northern India.

Abstract: Abstract The pursuit of general C(sp3)–H amination methods using alkylamines, the most accessible and desirable nitrogen sources, represents a long-standing challenge in synthetic chemistry. This challenge is particularly acute in the context of late-stage peptide modification, where the incorporation of pharmaceutically privileged alkylamines such as piperidines and morpholines remains promising but largely underdeveloped. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed, picolinamide (PA)-directed C(sp3)–H amination protocol that enables the direct, site-selective installation of abundant secondary alkylamines onto the α-position of N-terminal glycine residues in peptides. This method operates under mild, robust, operationally simple conditions and exhibits broad substrate scope (>50 peptide examples), with its synthetic utility highlighted by the direct construction of linker-free peptide-drug conjugates (PDCs) as well as seamless integration with solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). Detailed mechanistic insights from spectroscopic studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support a pathway involving N-centered radical formation and a key N-acylimine intermediate. Notably, the secondary alkylamine serves as both radical precursor and nucleophile, facilitating access to high-valent Cu(III) intermediates and nucleophile addition steps in the catalytic cycle, respectively. Furthermore, this method allows modulation of peptide pharmacokinetic properties and exhibits promising anticancer activity in select PDCs, underscoring its potential for peptide-based medicinal chemistry.
Author: Xiao, Jingran
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Copper-Catalyzed Late-Stage C(sp3)–H Amination of N-Terminal Glycine Peptides with Secondary Alkylamines

Abstract: Abstract The disorder–order transition of metal alloys delivers ordered intermetallic nanoparticles (NPs) as efficient and stable catalysts. However, this transition is practically challenging due to the thermodynamically low driving force and the complex kinetic competition with concurrent processes (e.g., phase separation). Here, we report a kinetic-controlled phase-capturing strategy for ordering multimetallic NPs via pulsed heating treatment. This strategy enables the rapid and universal synthesis of intermetallic NPs with varying elemental compositions (up to eight elements) and stoichiometric ratios in seconds (<10 pulses, down to 1 pulse). In situ transmission electron microscopy reveals a multistep transformation pathway, where disordered NPs premelt at the heating stage of each pulse and subsequently recrystallize toward metastable intermediate states or the final ordered structures via short-range atomic diffusion in the cooling stage. This work develops a promising concept for controllably synthesizing complex intermetallic NPs, as well as for obtaining versatile metastable structures in nanomaterials.
Author: Huang, Jiawei
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Kinetic-Controlled Ultrafast Synthesis of Ordered Intermetallic Nanoparticles

Abstract: Abstract Although technologically promising for producing petrochemicals directly from renewable resources, CO2 hydrogenation to methanol remains a formidable challenge due to the activity-selectivity trade-off. Current industrial copper-based catalysts often generate substantial CO byproducts that limit CO2 utilization efficiency. Herein, we report a highly active and selective Cu/amorphous ZrO2 (Cu/a-ZrO2) catalyst by using a modified solvothermal method, which achieves a space-time methanol productivity of up to ∼1560 gmethanol kgcat–1 h–1 with a high methanol selectivity of ∼76% at 260 °C. The strategic integration of in situ synchrotron-based vacuum ultraviolet photoionization mass spectrometry (SVUV-PIMS), multimodal in situ/operando infrared spectroscopies, kinetic isotope experiments, and computational studies collectively demonstrate that the direct dissociation of C–O bond in CO2 generates *CO followed by subsequent hydrogenation to methanol via relay catalysis on adjacent Cu+–ZrOx and Cu0 dual sites, which subsequently promote the initial activation step of CO2 and the subsequent hydrogenation steps of *CO to methanol, respectively. We confirm that methanol synthesis follows a *CO-mediated mechanism on these sites, highlighting the origin of the excellent performance of self-designed Cu/a-ZrO2.
Author: Liu, Tangkang
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: CO-Mediated Relay Catalysis Affords Selective CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol

Abstract: Abstract The emergence of covalent organic framework (COF) nanotubes extends tubular materials from rigid atomic networks to flexible molecular frameworks, yet their thermal transport properties remain unexplored. Here, based on an experimentally synthesized two-dimensional pentagonal COF (penta-COF), we construct a series of one-dimensional nanotubes and systematically investigate their axial thermal conductivity (κaxial) across the curvature and chirality parameter spaces. Using molecular dynamics simulations powered by a fine-tuned universal machine-learning potential, we uncover an anomalous curvature-enhanced thermal transport (κaxial ∼ 1/R1.31), opposite to the curvature-suppressed behavior commonly observed in conventional atom-based nanotubes. Moreover, at nearly constant radius, κaxial exhibits a pronounced dependence on chirality. Structural and vibrational analyses reveal that curvature acts as a geometric confinement field that suppresses disordered vibrations of flexible organic linkers and enhances conformational ordering, thereby improving the transport efficiency of low-frequency phonons. Further symmetry-guided analysis shows that the chirality dependence originates from a competition between the chirality-induced axial-misalignment penalty associated with the intrinsic elastic anisotropy of the pentagonal parent lattice and the conformational-ordering enhancement induced by rolling-driven symmetry reduction and strain homogenization. These findings reveal an unconventional geometry-phonon coupling mechanism in penta-COF nanotubes, and establish curvature and chirality as effective design parameters for tuning thermal transport in molecule-based one-dimensional pentagonal materials.
Author: Ma, Xinyuan
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Curvature-Enhanced and Chirality-Modulated Anomalous Thermal Transport in Pentagonal Covalent Organic Framework Nanotubes

Abstract: Abstract Solid-state batteries (SSBs) promise higher energy density and improved safety, but interparticle voids and unstable solid–solid interfaces still limit their performance. Here, we translate the concept of lubrication into an electrolyte-lubrication strategy for SSBs. We design a solvation-tailored electrolyte lubricant, termed ACE (aggregate cluster electrolyte), in which spatially structured ion-pair clusters direct interphase formation. In ACE, molecular-orbital reconfiguration within Li+–anion clusters favors the growth of a thin, electronically insulating, inorganic-rich solid–liquid electrolyte interphase (SLEI) on sulfide electrolytes, mitigating their intrinsic instability. The fluid ACE infiltrates interparticle voids, forming percolating Li+-conduction networks and facilitating dynamic reconstruction of the solid–electrolyte interphase during cycling. These attributes enable stable Li-metal cycling at reduced external pressure and enhance cathode active-material utilization. Electrochemical–thermal simulations further show that ACE homogenizes ionic fluxes and thermal gradients at the cell scale. Electrolyte lubrication thus emerges as a scalable interfacial-engineering approach for making sulfide-based SSBs operate under more practical conditions.
Author: Kim, Won-Yeong
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Electrolyte Lubricants for Solid-State Batteries

Abstract: Abstract Small aminoorganosulfonates are reservoirs of carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur in marine and host-associated ecosystems. Homotaurine, a C3-aminoorganosulfonate produced by marine algae and present in algal-derived foods, is comparatively well documented, but its complete microbial catabolism has remained unresolved. Here we identify a complete bacterial pathway for homotaurine catabolism in Caballeronia jiangsuensis strain McCoy, isolated by metabolic enrichment from soil by growth on homotaurine. Growth, proteomic, metabolomic, biochemical, structural, and heterologous-expression analyses show that homotaurine is imported and oxidatively deaminated to sulfopropanoate, then converted to sulfolactate through E-sulfoacrylate by SpuABCD and SpuIJ, enzymes related to succinate dehydrogenase and fumarase. Sulfolactate is cleaved by redundant SuyAB sulfolyases to release pyruvate and sulfite, which is oxidized and excreted as sulfate, completing biomineralization. Crystal structures of the HtaA homotaurine-binding protein and SuyAB2 sulfolyase reveal ligand recognition and provide a structural framework for sulfolactate cleavage. Hidden Markov model searches and Tara Oceans and human gut metagenomes show that the core sulfopropanoate-to-sulfolactate module is widespread in marine Proteobacteria, especially Roseobacter-lineage bacteria, and occurs more narrowly in human gut-associated sulfur-metabolizing taxa such as Bilophila wadsworthia. This pathway connects algal, dietary, and xenobiotic C3-aminoorganosulfonates to microbial carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycling, and identifies sulfopropanoate turnover as a conserved module in organosulfonate metabolism.
Author: Pallasdies, Luise
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: A Bacterial Pathway for Homotaurine Catabolism via Sulfopropanoate

Abstract: Abstract The species-selective SDH inhibitor siccanin presents unique opportunities for therapeutic development but suffers from poor physicochemical properties and challenging chemical problems. Here we report an approach to its synthesis that quickly intercepts its unusually hindered cis-syn-cis drimane core, i.e., its local chemical space. Computation helps rationalize and predict the reactivity, especially conformational preferences, configurational outcomes, and the reactivity of a key O-centered radical.
Author: Larisa P. Pop
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Synthesis of Siccanin by Computational Subtarget Selection

Abstract: Optical phased array (OPA)-based LiDAR technology provides high-speed, solid-state sensing for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and aerial systems. However, current OPA-based LiDAR platforms lack the ability to accurately recognize and classify materials, limiting their effectiveness for advanced scene understanding in robotics and machine perception. Here, we propose a method for OPA-based LiDAR that integrates a silicon photonic OPA chip with a polarisation-resolved optical neural network (PolarONN) chip to directly analyse the polarisation of backscattered signals. This integrated architecture enables a polarization-resolved point-cloud output by jointly providing 3D geometry, return intensity, and a polarization-derived attribute, and it attaches a point-wise material label inferred by the on-chip PolarONN. Compared to representative electronic classification back-ends used for polarization-based material identification, our on-chip photonic inference core provides ns-scale response with a low electrical power budget for the inference module. We experimentally demonstrate robust, real-time classification of three representative materials (wood, stone, and steel) with classification accuracies exceeding 85%, at distances up to 10 meters. Our study establishes a practical route toward real-time polarisation-resolved LiDAR perception, significantly enhancing the capabilities of next-generation autonomous sensing technologies. This study combines an optical phasedarray LiDAR with an integrated photonic neural network to map three-dimensional scenes and classify materials using polarization-resolved optical echoes.
Author: Wang, Zihao
Title: Optical phased array LiDAR chips towards polarization-resolved 4D sensing

Abstract: Abstract Enduring relationships dramatically shape behaviors by promoting affiliation between familiar individuals; however, the neural mechanisms driving attachments remain unclear. Oxytocin receptor (Oxtr) signaling in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) reinforces pair bond formation in socially monogamous prairie voles. How Oxtr influences NAc activity during affiliative behaviors with partners and rejection of strangers is unknown. Using in vivo fiber photometry, we demonstrate that genetic loss of Oxtr sex-specifically disrupts attachment behaviors and associated NAc activity. In females, loss of Oxtr reduces prosocial behaviors and NAc activity during initial chemosensory investigation of novel males; however, partner-directed affiliative behavior and associated activity increase independently of Oxtr. In males, loss of Oxtr increases prosocial investigation of novel females, and initial behavioral and neural activity patterns predict future partner preference in Oxtr-null males. These findings reveal sex-specific roles for Oxtr in early pair bond development through modulation of prosociality and sensory processing.
Author: Kimberly L. P. Long
Title: Loss of oxytocin receptor function disrupts neural signatures of pair bonding and fidelity in the nucleus accumbens

Abstract: Abstract Brain vascular barriers are dysfunctional in many neurological disorders, including Huntington’s disease (HD), but which vessels are affected and how remains unclear. Using in vivo two-photon microscopy in R6/2 HD-model mice, we reveal a striking divergence in barrier dysfunction. Surface vessels of the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB) drive pathology in HD by paracellular leakage, while parenchymal vessels forming the blood-brain barrier (BBB) exhibit increased vesicular transport and adsorptive-mediated transcytosis (AMT), with arterioles representing the most critically impacted vascular segment. The pathology of both barriers was spatially-matched with astrocyte activation pattern localized to affected vessels both in R6/2 mice and in brains of HD patients. Sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1pr1) agonist treatment reversed BCSFB leakage and partially restored BBB function, selectively reducing AMT in arterioles, with no effect in capillaries and venules. These findings redefine HD vascular pathology, demonstrating heterogeneous, vessel-type-specific barrier failure beyond generalized “disruption,” uncovering mechanistic vulnerabilities and the therapeutic potential of S1pr1 modulation.
Author: Kucharz, Krzysztof
Title: Huntington’s disease vasculopathy is barrier-type-selective and arteriolar-dominant with spatially-coupled astrogliosis and reversible by S1pr1 stimulation

Abstract: Tumor-targeting cytokines have emerged as a promising strategy for cancer immunotherapy, although their mechanisms of action often remain complex. In this study, we develop an approach by combining tumor-targeted IL-10 (CmAb-(IL10)2) with IL-2 (CmAb-IL2) to enhance antitumor immunity while minimizing immune-related adverse events (irAEs). We demonstrate that endogenous IL-10 plays a critical role in IL-2-mediated antitumor effects, and that the combination of CmAb-(IL10)2 and CmAb-IL2 preferentially expands less-exhausted CD8+ T cells within tumors. Mechanistically, we identify that the IL-10/IL-10 receptor (IL-10R) axis in dendritic cells (DCs) is critical for mediating the efficacy of this combination therapy by promoting intratumoral DC function. Furthermore, we show that this combination enhances antitumor immune responses in humanized female mice and ex vivo patient-derived tumor fragments models. Our findings reveal that tumor-targeted IL-10 synergizes with IL-2 to enhance antitumor immunity through the IL-10/IL-10R/DC axis within tumors, while mitigating IL-2-associated irAEs through the IL-10/IL-10R/macrophage axis. This approach offers an IL-10 based strategy to improve the efficacy of immunotherapy while reducing irAEs. IL2-based immunotherapies enhance anti-tumor immune responses, however, there is a significant risk of severe immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Here the authors show that combining a tumor-targeting cetuximab-based bispecific IL10 fusion protein with tumor-targeted IL2 enhances antitumor immunity and controls tumor growth while reducing IL2-associated irAEs through distinct IL-10R functions in dendritic cells and macrophages.
Author: Sun, Zhichen
Title: Tumor-targeted IL-10 synergizes with IL-2 to enhance antitumor immunity while minimizing immune-related adverse events

Abstract: Photoelectrochemical water splitting is a promising pathway for renewable solar fuel production. The photoelectrochemical performance strongly depends on the charge separation ability within the space charge layer. In space charge layer, the charge dynamics should be governed by band bending profile consisting with built-in electric field and space charge layer width, yet the precise mechanisms remain unclear. Herein, using Sn doping to regulate band bending profile of Fe2O3 photoanode, we disentangle the effect of space charge layer width and built-in electric field on charge dynamics in photoelectrochemical water splitting by in-situ time-resolved spectroscopies. Space charge layer width determines the onset of photogenerated charge separation, exhibiting a threshold of ~2.4 nm. Above WSCL threshold, the strong built-in electric field in Fe2O3 photoanode effectively empties the occupied electron trap states and blocks the recombination between the back electrons and charged intermediates, thereby facilitating surface hole accumulation for improving water oxidation reaction rate. Photoelectrochemical performance strongly depends on charge separation within space charge layer, but the precise mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors disentangle the effect of space charge layer width and built-in electric field on charge dynamics using in-situ time-resolved techniques.
Author: Li, Dongfeng
Subfield: Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment
Title: Disentangling the effect of space and electric field on photoelectrochemical water splitting

Abstract: Abstract Small RNAs (sRNAs) are widespread across diverse flowering plant species and play important roles regulating reproduction and environmental responses. However, how sRNAs exert their function is largely unknown, likely due to their typical origin in non-genic regions, the lack of distinct gene targets, and the sparse characterization of their associated Argonaute (AGO) effector proteins. Here we show that Arabidopsis male reproductive sRNAs associate with AGO4, 5, 6 and 9, all of which are enriched in meiocytes along with RNA Polymerase V (Pol V). This enables these sRNAs to methylate loci with imperfect sequence homology. AGO4, AGO6 and AGO9 predominantly load 24-nucleotide (nt) Pol IV-derived sRNAs and mediate DNA methylation in meiocytes in a dosage-dependent manner. Despite closer homology to microRNA-associated AGO1 and AGO10, AGO5 primarily binds CLSY3- and Pol IV-derived 21-24 nt sRNAs. Transcriptomic and methylomic analyses of meiocytes from single and compound ago mutants demonstrate distinct yet complementary roles of AGO4/6/9 and AGO5 in regulating protein-coding genes and silencing transposons in the germline. These molecular disruptions are accompanied by significant meiotic defects. Together, our findings reveal how AGO4/6/9-mediated DNA methylation and AGO5, likely acting through post-transcriptional gene silencing, work together to promote male germline development.
Author: Long, Jincheng
Title: Multiple Argonaute complexes orchestrate epigenetic silencing in the Arabidopsis germline

Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) metal oxides (MOs) are crucial materials in semiconductor optoelectronics and energy applications. Recently, ultra-confined and anisotropic polaritons, which are hybrid light-matter waves, in 2D MOs have renewed interest in the field of nanophotonics. With natural abundance, diverse compositions, and rich symmetries, MOs exhibit a wide range of electromagnetic responses from the visible to terahertz spectral range, providing various polariton platforms for designing on-chip photonic integrated circuits. In this Review, we discuss crystal symmetry and polaritons in MOs, present intrinsic and extrinsic manipulation approaches, and summarize strategies for synthesizing 2D polaritonic MOs. We also propose 2D MO-based polaritonic device architectures for use in heat management, photonics, and biosensing, all of which could be integrated into future photonic chips. Overall, with the rapid flourishing of 2D MO polaritonics, this review aims to stimulate further exploration and innovation for next-generation on-chip photonic systems. Metal oxides support a broad range of polaritons. In this review, the authors extend this to the emerging family of two-dimensional metal oxides and cover the impact of crystal structure and extrinsic manipulation on the polaritons along with synthesis approaches and future photonics applications.
Author: Zhong, Gang
Subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics
Title: Two-dimensional metal oxide polaritonics

Abstract: Although gait is often considered highly automated, cognitive performance may be associated with dynamic trunk–pelvis kinematics as locomotor demand increases. How these associations vary across standardized walking speeds remains unclear. This study examines speed-dependent associations between cognitive performance and DIERS-derived trunk–pelvis kinematics. Sixty-four healthy young adults completed four cognitive tests and DIERS Formetric 4Dmotion assessment during static standing and treadmill walking at 1, 2, 4, and 5 km/h. Eight trunk–pelvis kinematic variables were examined using correlation, trend, linear mixed-effects, principal component, and canonical correlation analyses. Cognition–kinematic associations were predominantly observed at the faster walking conditions of 4 and 5 km/h, with correlations involving PASAT and spinal-curvature measures reaching r = − 0.700 and r = − 0.709, respectively. Linear mixed-effects models identified significant Speed × SDMT interactions for sagittal imbalance (β = − 0.10, 95% CI − 0.14 to − 0.06; p < 0.001) and pelvic drop (β = − 0.12, 95% CI − 0.16 to − 0.08; p < 0.001), indicating smaller speed-related increases among participants with higher SDMT scores. Pelvic drop increased from 1.59 ± 0.63° during standing to 19.40 ± 7.89° at 5 km/h. The first principal component accounted for 53.4% and 68.7% of kinematic variance at 4 and 5 km/h, respectively. Exploratory multivariate analysis also identified a significant first cognitive–kinematic canonical function (r < sub > c < /sub > = 0.855, Wilks’ Λ = 0.185, F = 3.456, p < 0.001). Cognitive performance was associated with trunk–pelvis kinematic behavior primarily at faster walking speeds. Walking-speed variation may provide a useful framework for examining cognition–kinematic coupling; however, these findings do not establish causal cognitive control or direct mechanical gait instability.
Author: Al‐Sharman, Alham
Subfield: Physical Therapy, Sports Therapy and Rehabilitation
Title: Cognitive performance and dynamic spinopelvic kinematics across walking speeds in healthy young adults

Abstract: Complete removal of calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH) 2 ] prior to obturation is critical for optimal sealer penetration and long-term success of root canal treatment; however, its elimination from complex anatomical regions such as internal resorption cavities remains challenging. This study evaluated the effectiveness of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-and glycolic acid (GA)-based irrigation regimens with or without chitosan in removing Ca(OH) 2 from artificial internal resorption cavities. Sixty extracted human mandibular premolars were prepared, standardized artificial internal resorption cavities were created, and the specimens were filled with Ca(OH) 2 . The teeth were randomly allocated to four experimental groups (n = 15) according to the irrigation protocol: EDTA, EDTA + chitosan, GA, and GA + chitosan. Residual Ca(OH) 2 was evaluated using stereomicroscopic scoring and quantitative ImageJ analysis. For stereomicroscopic assessment, the tooth was considered the experimental unit, and the scores obtained from the two root halves of each tooth were combined to generate a tooth-level score. Data were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis test followed by the Dunn–Bonferroni post hoc test ( p < 0.05). Significant differences were observed among the experimental groups ( p < 0.001). The EDTA group exhibited the highest combined stereomicroscopic scores, whereas the GA + chitosan group showed the lowest scores. No statistically significant differences were observed between the EDTA and EDTA + chitosan groups or between the GA and GA + chitosan groups in the stereomicroscopic analysis. In contrast, both GA-based protocols demonstrated significantly lower residual Ca(OH) 2 than the EDTA-based protocols. Quantitative ImageJ analysis corroborated this pattern, with the GA + chitosan regimen showing the lowest percentage of residual Ca(OH) 2 surface coverage. Within the limitations of this in vitro study, GA-based irrigation regimens resulted in less residual Ca(OH) 2 than EDTA-based regimens, although the specific contribution of chitosan could not be established.
Author: Mıdoglu, Gubina
Title: Comparison of EDTA- and glycolic acid-based irrigation regimens with or without chitosan for calcium hydroxide removal from artificial internal resorption cavities: an in vitro study

Abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic disease associated with impaired renal function and electrolyte balance, which may contribute to an increased risk of renal and metabolic complications. This study aimed to evaluate and compare renal function tests (RFTs) (urea, uric acid, and creatinine) and electrolytes (Ca 2+ , Na + , K + , and Cl − ) in individuals with and without diabetic disease. A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted with 300 participants, including 150 diabetic patients and 150 healthy individuals. Demographic data and laboratory measurements of RFTs and electrolytes were collected. Univariate analysis was employed to compare the two groups; Pearson’s correlation coefficient was used to assess correlations between variables; and binary logistic regression was utilized to identify independent factors associated with diabetes. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Most demographic characteristics did not differ statistically between the two groups. Diabetic patients showed significantly higher levels of creatinine (0.5926 ± 0.2134 vs. 0.5463 ± 0.1284, P = 0.0242), urea (25.47 ± 8.986 vs. 22.25 ± 6.639, P = 0.0006), and K + (4.707 ± 0.5688 vs. 4.527 ± 0.3470, P = 0.0012), while the levels of Na + (137.4 ± 13.42 vs. 144.1 ± 3.496, P < 0.0001) and Ca 2+ (2.397 ± 0.1456 vs. 2.441 ± 0.06213, P = 0.0009) were lower in diabetic patients compared to healthy individuals, with the mean absolute magnitude of the differences limited. Pearson analysis revealed statistically significant weak positive, weak negative, and moderate negative correlations between RBG and urea ( r = 0.1713, P = 0.0415), creatinine ( r =-0.1623, P = 0.0496), and Na + r =-0.3644, P < 0.0001), respectively. Binary logistic regression analysis showed that urea (OR = 1.0522, 95% CI = 1.0166–1.0890, P = 0.0038), uric acid (OR = 0.6956, 95% CI = 0.5441–0.8894, P = 0.0038), Na + (OR = 0.9610, 95% CI = 0.9382–0.9843, P = 0.0011), and K + (OR = 1.8766, 95% CI = 1.0460–3.3667, P = 0.0348) were significant independent factors associated with diabetes. In conclusion, diabetic patients exhibit significant differences in some renal function and electrolyte indicators compared to healthy individuals, with a limited number of these indicators showing independent association with diabetes after multivariate analysis.
Author: Abdul Baset Abbas
Title: Evaluation of renal function tests and serum electrolytes in diabetic and non-diabetic individuals: a comparative cross-sectional study

Abstract: We propose a stochastic extension of a compartmental epidemiological model for COVID-19 to describe the transmission dynamics in Bogotá, Colombia. To account for intrinsic variability in infection, incubation, recovery, and vaccination processes, random perturbations are incorporated into key model parameters. The resulting system of stochastic differential equations is approximated using the Euler-Maruyama method, enabling likelihood-based parameter estimation. We derive an extended basic reproduction number, along with its associated uncertainty, providing a statistically grounded measure of epidemic potential under varying conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework successfully captures the variability observed in the epidemiological data and highlights the importance of accounting for parameter uncertainty in public health decision-making. The model is statistically tractable, computationally efficient, and adaptable to other infectious diseases and urban settings. Possible extensions include incorporating reinfection dynamics, integrating additional data sources, and using Bayesian inference to enhance uncertainty quantification.
Author: Ríos-Gutiérrez, Andrés
Title: Stochastic modeling for uncertainty quantification in COVID-19 dynamics using Euler Maruyama approximation

Abstract: The transition toward a low-carbon economy has intensified scrutiny on the environmental strategies of carbon-intensive sectors, such as the chemical industry. This paper examines the impact of green innovation on corporate financial performance (CFP), as empirical testing of the NRBV remains limited in such sectors, as well as the moderating role of advertising intensity in this relationship. In this study, advertising intensity refers to a firm's overall advertising expenditure relative to sales, which may include environmental and sustainability-related communication activities used to enhance stakeholder awareness, corporate legitimacy, and the market visibility of green initiatives. Using an unbalanced panel of 105 publicly listed chemical companies from 2015 to 2023, this study examines two dimensions of green innovation, namely, environmental performance-based innovation (EnvPS) and invention-based innovation (IS), and analyses their effects on return on equity (ROE), return on assets (ROA), and return on sales (ROS). The results of the panel regression indicate that the effect of green innovation on CFP is not significant in the short term, indicating a lack of market awareness of sustainability activities and slow returns on innovation. However, advertising intensity introduces a dual interacting role: it amplifies the financial gains associated with EnvPS, while concurrently weakening the profitability effects of IS due to increased short-term cost burdens. This study offers novel empirical evidence on how advertising intensity differentially conditions the relationship between innovation and performance in the global chemical industry, demonstrating that visibility, rather than innovation alone, is critical for converting sustainability investments into financial value.
Author: Hui Shan Lee
Title: Do green innovation and advertising intensity enhance financial performance? Firm-level evidence from the global chemical sector

Abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a stereoselective Morita–Baylis–Hillman protocol to access allylic γ-imino α-trifluoromethyl alcohol adducts. The reaction proceeds under mild and tunable conditions, enabling diastereodivergent access to the two possible stereoisomers through modulation of the Lewis base and additives. The synthetic interest of the resulting compounds as precursors of medicinally relevant fluorinated scaffolds has been demonstrated. A proposal for the reaction mechanism and the stereochemical induction has also been made.
Author: Sirvent, Ana
Title: Diastereodivergent Morita–Baylis–Hillman Reaction of α,β-Unsaturated N-tert -Butanesulfinyl Imines and Trifluoromethyl Ketones

Abstract: Abstract While prior studies indicate innovation and product introductions decrease during economic downturns and recessions, the nature of innovative entry by startups is unclear. Furthermore, studies of business entry, which is dominated by non-innovative firms, show mixed results. We build on innovation theories to propose that likelihood of entry varies with business cycle fluctuations, following an inverted U-shape relationship with startup innovativeness and with related contextual variations by level of economic development. Using GEM data to study entrepreneurial entry in 66 countries between 2003 and 2018—evaluating both the recovery from the dot.com crash and Global Financial Crisis—we find evidence supporting our proposed counter-cyclic disruption mechanism for discontinuously innovative entry, pro-cyclic prosperity pull mechanism for incrementally innovative entry, and counter-cyclic recession push mechanism for imitative entry, together with contextual variations with economic development.
Author: Steffens, Paul
Title: Innovative entrepreneurial entry over the business cycle: variation by form of innovation and country economic development

Abstract: Abstract Are some preprint platforms more attractive to predatory publishers than others? To explore this question, we analyze unsolicited messages received for a research paper spanning the social and health sciences. The paper was posted on two major preprint platforms: Research Square, which primarily serves the natural and health sciences, and the Social Science Research Network (SSRN), the leading platform for social sciences. Using an identification strategy that attributes differences in solicitation volume to platform-specific factors rather than the study’s characteristics, authors, or institutions, we find significant differences in the volume of predatory solicitations. Research Square received considerably more solicitations, mostly from non-social science disciplines such as clinical medicine and psychiatry. This suggests that predatory publishers not only target Research Square more frequently but are also attracted to disciplines with higher publication pressure and greater commercial potential. These findings provide researchers with a clearer understanding of the risks associated with different platforms and offer insights into avoiding predatory publishers.
Author: Keloharju, Matti
Title: Hunting grounds for predatory publishers

Abstract: This article employs a comparative feminist-postcolonial spatial close reading of Geetanjali Shree's Tomb of Sand and Arundhati Roy's The Ministry of Utmost Happiness to examine how South Asian women's fiction reimagines space, memory, and the gendered body as sites of resistance against social and ideological divisions. Employing Edward Soja's concept of Thirdspace, this article argues that both novels challenge hegemonic territoriality and expose the absurdity of man-made boundaries. The novels construct fluid and transformative spaces that destabilise dominant patriarchal ideological structures. The gendered body and memory enable the protagonists to dismantle social and national dichotomies and divisions. By bringing these novels into dialogue, the article contributes to feminist postcolonial debates on space and memory. Space is constructed in the novels as retrospective, i.e., recovering a cosmopolitan space-time matrix, or prospective, which builds a future on hope and inclusive community. Both function as alternative realms in which marginalised subjects resist hegemonic structures and reconfigure possibilities of coexistence and human connection.
Author: Manawar, Aniqua
Title: Beyond Boundaries: Feminist Thirdspace in Tomb of Sand and The Ministry of Utmost Happiness

Abstract: Introduction Pythium insidiosum keratitis is an emerging, vision-threatening corneal infection that is increasingly recognized worldwide, particularly in tropical and agrarian regions. Owing to its close clinical resemblance to fungal keratitis, delayed diagnosis and inappropriate antifungal therapy frequently result in rapid stromal destruction, therapeutic keratoplasty, and poor visual outcomes. Unlike true fungi, Pythium insidiosum is an oomycete lacking ergosterol in its cell membrane, rendering conventional antifungal agents largely ineffective and necessitating a paradigm shift toward targeted pharmacotherapy.Areas covered This review summarizes contemporary advances in the pharmacologic management of Pythium insidiosum keratitis, including mechanisms underlying antifungal resistance, current evidence supporting antibacterial-based therapy such as linezolid and azithromycin, adjunctive anti-collagenolytic and anti-inflammatory approaches, and emerging anti-oomycete therapeutics. Literature from PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science was reviewed to evaluate drug susceptibility patterns, translational therapeutic strategies, and evolving precision medicine approaches.Expert opinion Management of Pythium keratitis is transitioning from empirical antifungal therapy toward targeted anti-oomycete (antibacterial) treatment guided by rapid diagnostics and susceptibility profiling. Future advances will likely integrate molecular diagnostics, AI-assisted therapeutic prediction, nanotechnology-enabled drug delivery, and personalized pharmacologic and surgical strategies to improve globe salvage and visual outcomes.
Author: Gurnani, Bharat
Title: Pharmacotherapy of Pythium insidiosum keratitis – a contemporary update
